spec.name: Trend v32
spec.notes: Twelve-month return skipping the most recent weeks, long the strongest fifth.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.0, annual return 7%, maximum drawdown 4%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.03 to 2.13 (change +0.11).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.03 to 0.09. Changed by strict mode: operators zscore_full.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.98 (as submitted, 5 bps: 2.03); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.01.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.03 against 2.03 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is 0.47 against 2.03 in research, a gap of +1.55.
The best year gives 19% of total P&L (year 5) and calm regimes give 46%; Sharpe is 1.43 in calm and 3.66 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.00, so the claimed 2.00 becomes 2.00 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.07 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.01, 95th percentile 0.48).
Perturbing the 1 numeric value in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.03 to as low as 1.28 (as low as 1.82 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (20 days) give 31% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 17% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (pit_replay EX-2, holdout_test EX-5).
